types.oie_definition: A commercial business organization.
types.embedding_query_text: Company: A commercial business organization. Also called corporation, firm, business, enterprise.

chosen_type.label: Corporation
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type and mentions clearly refer to commercial business organizations, which is precisely what Corporation represents, explicitly listing 'company' as an alias and 'Microsoft Corporation' as an example.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

candidates.label: Store
candidates.comment: A retail business that sells goods to consumers. Also called shop, retail outlet, boutique, market. Examples: a grocery store, a clothing store, an electronics store, a bookstore.

types.oie_definition: A numerical quantity representing the number of employment positions.
types.embedding_query_text: Job Count: A numerical quantity representing the number of employment positions. Also called number of positions, staff count, employee total.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type and mentions represent measurable amounts of employment positions, which aligns with the definition of Quantity as a data type for measurable amounts.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: JobPosting
candidates.comment: A JobPosting is an intangible listing that describes an open position within an organization. Also called job advertisement, employment listing, career opening. Examples: a software engineer job posting, a marketing manager vacancy, a retail associate opening.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: EmploymentAgency
candidates.comment: An EmploymentAgency is a LocalBusiness that helps individuals find jobs and employers find suitable candidates. Also called recruitment agency, staffing firm, job placement service. Examples: A temporary staffing agency, an executive search firm, a headhunting company.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

types.oie_definition: A specific business unit within a larger company focused on video games.
types.embedding_query_text: Gaming Division: A specific business unit within a larger company focused on video games. Also called game unit, interactive entertainment division, gaming arm.

chosen_type.label: GamingDivision
chosen_type.definition: A business unit within a larger company focused on video games.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org type accurately represents a business unit focused on gaming; 'Xbox' in this context refers to such a division, not a game or series.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: VideoGame
candidates.comment: An electronic game that involves human interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device. Also called computer game, console game, digital game. Examples: Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Call of Duty.

candidates.label: Casino
candidates.comment: A local business primarily offering gambling activities and often entertainment. Also called gambling house, gaming establishment, resort casino. Examples: Bellagio, Caesars Palace, Monte Carlo Casino.

candidates.label: VideoGameClip
candidates.comment: A short segment or part of a video game, often used for promotional or highlight purposes. Also called game clip, gameplay footage, video game segment. Examples: a highlight reel from an e-sports match, a trailer showing a game's cutscene, a short recording of a player's achievement.

candidates.label: Chapter
candidates.comment: A distinct section or division within a larger creative work, typically a book. Also called book section, segment, part, installment. Examples: Chapter 1 of "Moby Dick", the introduction chapter, the final chapter.

types.oie_definition: An individual human being.
types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called individual, human, figure.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type and mentions directly correspond to the Schema.org Person type, which represents an individual human being.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: ProfilePage
candidates.comment: A ProfilePage is a WebPage dedicated to displaying information about a specific entity, such as a person or organization. Also called user profile, personal page, bio page. Examples: a LinkedIn profile, a social media user's page, an author's biography page, a company's "About Us" page.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

types.oie_definition: The name of a specific position held by an employee within an organization.
types.embedding_query_text: Job Title: The name of a specific position held by an employee within an organization. Also called position, role, designation.

chosen_type.label: EmployeeRole
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type and mentions describe specific positions held by employees, which is precisely what EmployeeRole represents as a subclass of OrganizationRole.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

candidates.label: JobPosting
candidates.comment: A JobPosting is an intangible listing that describes an open position within an organization. Also called job advertisement, employment listing, career opening. Examples: a software engineer job posting, a marketing manager vacancy, a retail associate opening.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

types.oie_definition: A company or team that creates video games.
types.embedding_query_text: Game Development Studio: A company or team that creates video games. Also called game developer, dev studio, software house (gaming).

chosen_type.label: GameDevelopmentStudio
chosen_type.definition: A company or team that creates video games.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org type represents a company or team that develops video games; the candidates are for games or series, not organizations.

candidates.label: VideoGame
candidates.comment: An electronic game that involves human interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device. Also called computer game, console game, digital game. Examples: Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Call of Duty.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: Game
candidates.comment: A Game is a CreativeWork representing a rule-governed recreational activity, often involving players assuming roles in a fictional setting. Also called pastime, play, recreational activity. Examples: A board game like Chess, a video game like Minecraft, a role-playing game like Dungeons & Dragons, a card game like Poker.

candidates.label: VideoGameClip
candidates.comment: A short segment or part of a video game, often used for promotional or highlight purposes. Also called game clip, gameplay footage, video game segment. Examples: a highlight reel from an e-sports match, a trailer showing a game's cutscene, a short recording of a player's achievement.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

types.oie_definition: An online service or website that allows users to create and share content or to participate in social networking.
types.embedding_query_text: Social Media Platform: An online service or website that allows users to create and share content or to participate in social networking. Also called social network, online community, media site.

chosen_type.label: SocialMediaPlatform
chosen_type.definition: An online service or website that allows users to create and share content or to participate in social networking.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org type represents a social media platform itself; candidates are for content on platforms or enumerations of platforms, not instances of the platform.

candidates.label: SocialMediaPosting
candidates.comment: A creative work published on a social media platform, such as a blog post, tweet, or Facebook update. Also called social post, microblog post, status update, online share. Examples: a tweet from a celebrity, a Facebook status update, a blog post on Medium, an Instagram caption.

candidates.label: DiscussionForumPosting
candidates.comment: A social media posting that is an entry or message within an online discussion forum. Also called Forum post, message board entry, thread reply, online discussion. Examples: A question posted on a tech support forum, a comment in a gaming community thread, a new topic started on a hobby board. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically a longer, standalone article on a blog.

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.

candidates.label: BlogPosting
candidates.comment: An Article that is an individual entry or post published within a blog. Also called blog post, blog entry, weblog post. Examples: "A blog post about new software features", "An article on a travel blog", "A recipe post on a food blog". Distinct from Blog, which is the collection of posts.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

types.oie_definition: The application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes, especially in industry.
types.embedding_query_text: Technology: The application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes, especially in industry. Also called tech, innovation, applied science.

chosen_type.label: TechnologyConcept
chosen_type.definition: A field of study or application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org type represents 'technology' as a broad concept or field; candidates are for articles about technology, specific software, or generic products.

candidates.label: TechArticle
candidates.comment: An article providing technical information, such as how-to guides, troubleshooting steps, or specifications. Also called technical guide, how-to article, procedural document, specification. Examples: an article on 'How to install Linux', a troubleshooting guide for a software error, a specification document for a new API.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: Service
candidates.comment: An intangible offering provided by an organization, such as delivery, consulting, or repair. Also called offering, provision, assistance, support. Examples: a car repair service, a legal consulting service, a package delivery service, a web hosting service.

types.oie_definition: A segment of the economy that produces similar goods or services.
types.embedding_query_text: Industry Sector: A segment of the economy that produces similar goods or services. Also called economic segment, market sector, business area.

chosen_type.label: IndustrySector
chosen_type.definition: A segment of the economy that produces similar goods or services.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org type represents an abstract 'industry sector'; candidates are for specific businesses or products, not the economic segment itself.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: EntertainmentBusiness
candidates.comment: An EntertainmentBusiness is a LocalBusiness that provides entertainment services. Also called amusement business, leisure provider. Examples: A movie theater, a concert venue, an arcade, a theme park.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

types.oie_definition: A duration of time, often unspecified in exact length.
types.embedding_query_text: Time Period: A duration of time, often unspecified in exact length. Also called duration, interval, span of time.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type and mentions refer to a length or period of time, which is directly captured by the Schema.org Duration type.

mentions: Little more than a year later

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: InstantaneousEvent
candidates.comment: An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence. Examples: a computer log entry, a timestamp, a single click on a webpage. Distinct from Event, which typically has a duration.

types.oie_definition: A period of 365 or 366 days, typically from January 1 to December 31.
types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 or 366 days, typically from January 1 to December 31. Also called calendar year, annum.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: A year is a specific calendar date, and Schema.org's Date type can represent dates of various granularities, including year-only values.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

types.oie_definition: A series of related video games sharing a common brand, characters, or setting.
types.embedding_query_text: Video Game Franchise: A series of related video games sharing a common brand, characters, or setting. Also called game series, gaming IP, game saga.

chosen_type.label: VideoGameSeries
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type and mentions directly match VideoGameSeries, which explicitly includes 'game franchise' as an alias and provides relevant examples.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: Series
candidates.comment: A general group of related items, which may or may not be of the same kind, forming a sequence or collection. Also called collection, sequence, set, installment. Examples: a book series, a lecture series, a product line, a collection of artworks. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is a series of creative works.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeries
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeries is an ordered collection of related published materials, such as books, periodicals, TV shows, or video games. Also called series, collection, franchise, saga. Examples: "Harry Potter" book series, "Star Wars" movie series, "The Simpsons" TV series, "The Legend of Zelda" video game series. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeason, which is a single installment within a series.

candidates.label: MovieSeries
candidates.comment: A MovieSeries, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a collection of related movies. Also called film series, movie franchise, film saga. Examples: The Lord of the Rings trilogy, the James Bond film series, the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a short segment of a single movie.

candidates.label: VideoGame
candidates.comment: An electronic game that involves human interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device. Also called computer game, console game, digital game. Examples: Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Call of Duty.

types.oie_definition: A classification of goods or services based on their characteristics or function.
types.embedding_query_text: Product Category: A classification of goods or services based on their characteristics or function. Also called goods classification, item type, merchandise group.

chosen_type.label: SomeProducts
chosen_type.justification: SomeProducts is a placeholder for multiple similar products of the same kind and explicitly lists 'product category' as an alias, fitting the OIE type and mentions.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: CategoryCode
candidates.comment: A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code. Examples: UNSPSC code for office supplies, NAICS code for manufacturing, a product category ID.

candidates.label: ProductCollection
candidates.comment: A ProductCollection is a Collection of products, either ProductGroups or specific variants, listed together, often within an Offer. Also called product assortment, product bundle, product set. Examples: a collection of books by an author, a bundle of software products, a set of kitchen utensils, a curated selection of wines.

types.oie_definition: A classification for a facility used to house computer systems and associated components.
types.embedding_query_text: Data Center Type: A classification for a facility used to house computer systems and associated components. Also called server farm classification, computing facility type.

chosen_type.label: DataCenter
chosen_type.definition: A facility used to house computer systems and associated components.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org type represents a data center facility; candidates are irrelevant or too broad.

candidates.label: DataType
candidates.comment: DataType is a fundamental classification for the kind of values that can be stored or manipulated, such as numbers, text, or booleans. Also called primitive type, data format, value type. Examples: Integer, String, Boolean, Float, Date.

candidates.label: House
candidates.comment: A House is an accommodation type representing a building or structure intended for human or other creature habitation. Also called dwelling, residence, home. Examples: a single-family home, a townhouse, a cottage. Distinct from Apartment, which is a unit within a larger building, and HotelRoom, which is a temporary lodging unit.

candidates.label: LibrarySystem
candidates.comment: A LibrarySystem is an organization representing a collaborative network or system among several libraries. Also called library consortium, library network, regional library system. Examples: a state library system, a university library consortium, a public library district. Distinct from Library, which is a single physical or organizational entity.

candidates.label: OperatingSystem
candidates.comment: An OperatingSystem, as a SoftwareApplication, is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources. Also called OS, system software, platform. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a general application program.

candidates.label: RecyclingCenter
candidates.comment: A RecyclingCenter is a LocalBusiness providing facilities for recycling waste materials. Also called recycling facility, waste collection center. Examples: a municipal recycling center, a bottle and can redemption center, an electronics recycling drop-off, a hazardous waste collection site.

types.oie_definition: A named day within a seven-day cycle.
types.embedding_query_text: Day of the Week: A named day within a seven-day cycle. Also called weekday, weekend day.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type and mention directly correspond to the Schema.org DayOfWeek enumeration.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DaySpa
candidates.comment: A local business offering health and beauty services, typically without overnight accommodation. Also called Spa, beauty spa, wellness center. Examples: "The Serene Spa", "Urban Retreat Day Spa", "Relaxation Station". Distinct from HealthClub, which focuses more on fitness and exercise facilities.

types.oie_definition: A company or agency responsible for gathering, writing, and distributing news.
types.embedding_query_text: News Organization: A company or agency responsible for gathering, writing, and distributing news. Also called media outlet, press agency, news provider.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type and mention directly match NewsMediaOrganization, which represents an organization that produces and disseminates news, with 'BBC News' as an example.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

Examples: a highlight reel from an e-sports match, a trailer showing a game's cutscene, a short recording of a player's achievement.

candidates.label: Game
candidates.comment: A Game is a CreativeWork representing a rule-governed recreational activity, often involving players assuming roles in a fictional setting. Also called pastime, play, recreational activity. Examples: A board game like Chess, a video game like Minecraft, a role-playing game like Dungeons & Dragons, a card game like Poker.

candidates.label: PlayGameAction
candidates.comment: PlayGameAction is a ConsumeAction specifically representing the act of playing a video game. Also called gaming, video gaming, playing a digital game. Examples: playing "Minecraft", playing "Fortnite", playing "Chess" online, playing a mobile game. Distinct from PlayAction, which is a broader act of playing or performing.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

types.oie_definition: A company that conducts studies and analysis to provide insights and information.
types.embedding_query_text: Research Firm: A company that conducts studies and analysis to provide insights and information. Also called analysis company, consultancy, market research agency.

chosen_type.label: ResearchOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type and mention directly match ResearchOrganization, which represents an organization dedicated to conducting research, explicitly including 'research company' as an alias.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: Researcher
candidates.comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnPolicy
candidates.comment: An intangible providing information about product return policies associated with an organization, product, or offer. Also called return policy, refund policy, merchandise return terms. Examples: "30-day return policy", "final sale policy", "return policy for electronics".

candidates.label: AnalysisNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that combines factual reporting with the author's expertise, offering interpretations and conclusions. Also called news analysis, interpretive news, expert commentary. Examples: An article analyzing the economic impact of a new policy, a piece interpreting election results, a report on scientific findings with expert commentary. Distinct from NewsArticle, which primarily focuses on factual reporting without extensive interpretation.

types.oie_definition: Creations of the mind, such as inventions; literary and artistic works; designs; and symbols, names and images used in commerce.
types.embedding_query_text: Intellectual Property: Creations of the mind, such as inventions; literary and artistic works; designs; and symbols, names and images used in commerce. Also called IP rights, copyrights, patents.

chosen_type.label: CreativeWork
chosen_type.justification: CreativeWork is the most generic type of intellectual creation and explicitly lists 'intellectual property' as an alias in its definition.

candidates.label: CreativeWork
candidates.comment: A CreativeWork is the most generic type of intellectual or artistic creation, encompassing a wide range of media and forms. Also called artistic work, intellectual property, creation, content. Examples: A novel, a film, a photograph, a piece of software, a song, a painting.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeries
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeries is an ordered collection of related published materials, such as books, periodicals, TV shows, or video games. Also called series, collection, franchise, saga. Examples: "Harry Potter" book series, "Star Wars" movie series, "The Simpsons" TV series, "The Legend of Zelda" video game series. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeason, which is a single installment within a series.

candidates.label: DefinedTermSet
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a collection of formally defined terms, such as a glossary, dictionary, or classification scheme. Also called Glossary, vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, enumeration. Examples: The Dewey Decimal Classification system, a medical dictionary, a list of product categories, a set of industry standards. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a single entry within such a set.

candidates.label: Book
candidates.comment: A CreativeWork consisting of a written or printed work, typically bound together and protected by a cover. Also called publication, volume, printed matter. Examples: "To Kill a Mockingbird", "The Lord of the Rings", "A textbook on physics". Distinct from BookSeries, which is a collection of books.

candidates.label: Brand
candidates.comment: A Brand is an Intangible entity representing a name, symbol, or design used by an organization to identify and distinguish its products or services. Also called product line, trademark, label, marque. Examples: Nike, Apple, Coca-Cola, Google.

types.oie_definition: A business model where a customer pays a recurring price for access to a product or service.
types.embedding_query_text: Subscription Service: A business model where a customer pays a recurring price for access to a product or service. Also called membership service, recurring service, pay-per-use service.

chosen_type.label: SubscriptionService
chosen_type.definition: A business model where a customer pays a recurring price for access to a product or service.
chosen_type.justification: While 'Service' is a parent, no existing Schema.org type specifically captures the concept of a 'subscription service' as a business model.

candidates.label: PaymentService
candidates.comment: A PaymentService, as a FinancialProduct, is a service to transfer funds between persons or organizations. Also called money transfer service, payment processing service, remittance service. Examples: PayPal, Western Union, a bank's wire transfer service. Distinct from BankAccount, which is an account, not a service.

candidates.label: SubscribeAction
candidates.comment: The act of forming a unidirectional connection to receive continuous updates from an object or entity. Also called subscribing, following for updates, signing up for notifications. Examples: subscribing to a YouTube channel, signing up for a newsletter, subscribing to a podcast. Distinct from FollowAction, which implies a more reciprocal or social connection. Distinct from RegisterAction, which is a one-time enrollment.

candidates.label: CableOrSatelliteService
candidates.comment: A CableOrSatelliteService is a Service that provides access to media programming, such as TV or radio, delivered via cable or satellite infrastructure. Also called pay TV service, satellite radio provider, broadcast subscription service. Examples: Comcast Xfinity, DirecTV, SiriusXM Satellite Radio.

candidates.label: Service
candidates.comment: An intangible offering provided by an organization, such as delivery, consulting, or repair. Also called offering, provision, assistance, support. Examples: a car repair service, a legal consulting service, a package delivery service, a web hosting service.

candidates.label: TaxiService
candidates.comment: A local business or service offering vehicles for hire with drivers for local transportation, typically charging based on distance. Also called cab company, taxi provider, ride-hailing service. Examples: 'Yellow Cab Co.', 'Uber', 'Lyft', a local taxi firm. Distinct from Taxi, which refers to an instance of the service or the vehicle itself.

types.oie_definition: A specific day of the year, often including the month and year.
types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific day of the year, often including the month and year. Also called calendar date, specific day, point in time.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type and mention directly correspond to the Schema.org Date data type, representing a specific calendar date.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.
